body:
bd-01M19956MFSG7076QE4J66T7E9 (supportWeight publishes 'fully supported' on an empty eligible set) -
I HAVE DONE THE ANALYSIS WITHOUT TOUCHING THE CODE, so whoever you assign it to starts from a shape
rather than from my one-line finding. If that is me, say so and I will take it; if it is not, this
is theirs to use.

THE DEFECT IS A SENTINEL COLLISION, AND THE RANGE IS ALREADY FULLY SPOKEN FOR:

  cost.scala:359  `unassessable` sets supportWeight = 0.0   -> 0.0 MEANS "nothing supported"
  cost.scala:834  supportOf returns 1.0 when eligible.isEmpty
  cost.scala:836  supportOf returns 1.0 when wEligible <= 0
  cost.scala:838  supportOf returns 1.0 on genuinely full support

So 1.0 is simultaneously THE MAXIMUM OF A MEASURED SCALE and THE VALUE MEANING "NOBODY DECLARED
ELIGIBILITY". A consumer reading supportWeight = 1.0 cannot tell "every eligible term was measured"
from "eligibility was never stated". Those are opposite epistemic situations and they are the same
byte. The docstring at :296 tells the consumer to use exactly this field to notice or refuse - "a
consumer comparing costs across cells with different support is comparing claims of different
strength" - so the collision lands precisely on the one number we told people to trust.

AND THERE IS A SECOND MOUTH ON THE SAME HOLE, which I had not reported:

  cost.scala:300   supportWeight: Double = 1.0

A DEFAULT OF FULL SUPPORT. Any CostBreakdown built without naming its support claims it measured
everything. That is the same defect the chief named in PlacementResolution ("the default cannot
lie") and it is the reason I gave excludedBy no silent default there. The wire path is already
correct - AlignWire.costBreakdown takes supportWeight with NO default, deliberately, and codec v2
makes it REQUIRED on the wire - so the hole is the in-memory constructor only.

THE REMEDY, and it is the one the bead title already gestures at:

  supportWeight: Estimate[Double]      Measured(w) | Missing(reason)

`Estimate` is the module's existing carrier and this is exactly ADR 0003 - support travels with the
value, Missing is not a number. An external state has no eligible chart or structural terms, so its
support is not 1.0 and not 0.0; it is NOT APPLICABLE, and Missing(NotApplicable) says so. Then:

  - the default disappears, because Estimate has no natural default and callers must state one
  - "eligibility undeclared" becomes Missing(Unknown), distinguishable from Measured(1.0)
  - unassessable keeps Measured(0.0), which is a real measurement and should stay a number
  - the wire already requires the field, so v3 carries a discriminator rather than a bare double

WHAT I WOULD NOT DO: change scaleToEligible. Its 1.0 on an empty eligible set is DEFENSIBLE and
documented - refusing to scale a caller who never declared eligibility is the conservative act, and
the comment records that scaling over all terms collapsed every row to External. That one returns a
FACTOR, not a published claim. Only supportOf publishes.

COST: the field is read in wire.scala:314/334/411 and codec/align.scala:104, all of which already
handle Estimate elsewhere. It is a v3 wire bump. Not a small change, but a mechanical one.

Vision note, since it is why I keep circling this bead: "which words support each conclusion" is the
line in vision.md, and supportWeight IS that number for the alignment. A support of 1.0 that can
mean "we never looked" is the same failure as the imputed 0.5 I closed in 0ca09c5, one level up -
the value is honest and its PROVENANCE is missing.
